store.tagline: An OpenStreetMap that loads only when a visitor asks for it.
store.longDescription:
Privacy Map shows where you are without handing your visitors to a map company the moment they open a page.

Until somebody clicks Show map, the map is a placeholder drawn by the page itself: your place name, your address and a button. No iframe, image, script or font comes from another site, so there is nothing to ask consent for. One click loads the real OpenStreetMap, with your pin, zoom controls and the usual attribution. A short note under the button says what happens next.

Type [map] on any page where the map should go, or pick a page, such as contact, and the map is added at the end of it. Set the location by pasting a link from openstreetmap.org or coordinates like 52.3731, 4.8922, then choose a zoom and a height. The button takes a colour of your choice.

If you like, the plugin can remember a visitor's choice in their own browser, so maps show straight away on their next visit. It is off by default.

It is accessible and light: a real link that still leads to the map without JavaScript, a keyboard-friendly button with a visible focus ring, a labelled map frame, and well under a kilobyte of script.

It asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings. Without it no map is shown, because there is no location to show.

screenshots.caption: Before a click: your address on a placeholder, and nothing loaded from another site.
Close up: place name, address, a Show map button and a note on what it loads.
One click later: the real OpenStreetMap with your pin, on the same page.
The settings: place name, address, location, zoom, height and the page to add it to.
